main_body: Two stacked logs lying on their sides, with round cut ends facing left and long bark bodies running right
top_band: Only a thin 1-2 row lighter brown highlight along the upper log's back edge (rows ~3-5, x 9-18). It reads as a rounded bark edge, not a horizontal surface seen from above.
evidence: The logs are drawn in side profile. The circular cut ends are vertical faces seen face-on, and the bark runs off to the side as a flat dark body. No band reads as a top surface seen from above. There is no distinct front-edge line and no eave shadow. The only lighter strip along the upper log is 1-2 rows, which is a rim and not a surface. This matches the side-elevation failure in the guide.

style.evidence: The cut ends are well shaded, with cream, tan and brown rings in 4 steps. The bark bodies are mostly 2-3 flat dark browns, with large uniform areas of about 8x4 px and no grain or bark texture. The outline is a near-black brown on the dark side and is not clearly tinted to the material. Tiles carry fewer colours than the stall and well references, so the piece is thinner and flatter than the Beodeul standard.
